chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: Armed Forces Radio arranging and Mel Torme
summary: At Armed Forces Radio in Hollywood he arranged for Meredith Willson and Mel Torme, whom Horace praises for his harmony; the interviewer tells how Torme's drumming inspired him.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yes. I was with the Armed Forces Radio Service in Hollywood, and I did a lot of things for Maggie Whiteman.
Oh boy. You know, that guy knows a lot about harmony.
You want me to tell you a little

story here? How I got started in music? When I was a kid, I remember seeing a movie with him in which he didn't sing, he played drums, and I was so knocked out by his drum playing, that I decided that I want to be a drummer, and that was the first thing. That was Mel Torme.
Isn't that something? He can play the drums.
He can sit down and play you some chords on the piano too. You remember the Meltones?
That group. Oh man, now, he wrote a lot of stuff for them.
